sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Slievenamon is a hill of Irish myth. It rises in the east of Munster. Folk lore calls it the Hill of Fair Women. Old stories tell how the hero Fionn mac Cumhaill chose a wife by a footrace. Fionn desired a young partner. He stood on the cairn that crowns the hill and gave the signal. All the young women of the province ran toward him. Gráinne, the strong daughter of the king, outran every rival and reached the hilltop first. The tale links the mountain to the race and the brides who ran it. Some versions say Gráinne did not bear the promised sons. Others hold that after her lover died she returned and bore children for Fionn. The hill keeps the memory of the contest, the cairn, and the swift woman who won the field.
